For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the salmon came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.



<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as salmon

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers salmon in 4 forms kept separate in every comparison: salmon, as sold (255 results), salmon, canned (17 results), salmon, cooked (10 results) and salmon, powder or ground (2 results).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-salmon" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-salmon-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of salmon, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>3 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach salmon

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach salmon comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Salmon, as sold from escaped farmed salmon caught at sea (Norway) had total arsenic higher at 1,680 µg/kg, against 860 µg/kg for farmed salmon (Norway) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2020-pcbs-and-heavy-metals-in-farmed-escaped-and|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2020-pcbs-and-heavy-metals-in-farmed-escaped-and">PCBs and Heavy Metals in Farmed, Escaped and Wild</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2020-pcbs-and-heavy-metals-in-farmed-escaped-and">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, salmon, as sold from captured had total mercury higher at 18 µg/kg, against 17 µg/kg for all samples of species in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/brodziak-dopierala2023-mercury-fish-poland|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Brodziak-Dopierala B, Fischer A · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/brodziak-dopierala2023-mercury-fish-poland">Analysis of the Mercury Content in Fish for Human Consumption in Poland</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/brodziak-dopierala2023-mercury-fish-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2020-pcbs-and-heavy-metals-in-farmed-escaped-and|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2020-pcbs-and-heavy-metals-in-farmed-escaped-and">PCBs and Heavy Metals in Farmed, Escaped and Wild</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2020-pcbs-and-heavy-metals-in-farmed-escaped-and">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<a id="which-control-or-specification-choices-are-supported-and-which-are-policy-choices-requiring-separate-justification"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-030"></a>
<a id="what-supplier-process-or-test-result-changes-should-trigger-investigation-or-requalification"></a>

No maximum level for metals in salmon was verified from primary text for this page; buyers should confirm the limit that applies in the destination market.



<a id="finished-product-and-exposure-implications"></a>
## Exposure from salmon

<a id="hmi-ing-031"></a>
<a id="how-do-inclusion-rate-processing-yield-preparation-and-other-ingredients-affect-a-finished-product-estimate"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-032"></a>
<a id="how-do-consumption-patterns-and-intended-populations-affect-dietary-exposure-interpretation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-033"></a>
<a id="what-conclusions-require-finished-product-measurements-or-a-separate-exposure-assessment"></a>

No source in the library converted salmon concentrations into a verified estimate of intake for a defined population. Concentrations describe the food, not individual risk.

<a id="hmi-ing-034"></a>
<a id="which-primary-regulatory-instruments-apply-to-this-exact-ingredient-form-species-market-and-date"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-035"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-036"></a>
<a id="what-remains-unresolved-when-was-each-answer-reviewed-and-what-changed-in-this-version"></a>

Every source record that names salmon was decided on its content: 27 occurrence extracted, 27 records in all. The occurrence table renders every extracted result; held values remain visible with their reason.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.


<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Salmon FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-salmon" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-salmon" data-question="What heavy metals are found in salmon?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in salmon?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, uranium, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, Se, AsB, AsSugar-OH, AsSugar-PO4, AsSugar-SO3, AsSugar-SO4, DBT, DOT, oAs, OTC_sum_as_Sn, sumOTC, TBT, TPhT, TPT and unknown As in salmon, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-salmon" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-salmon" data-question="How do heavy metals get into salmon?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into salmon?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, salmon from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than salmon from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2020-pcbs-and-heavy-metals-in-farmed-escaped-and|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2020-pcbs-and-heavy-metals-in-farmed-escaped-and">PCBs and Heavy Metals in Farmed, Escaped and Wild</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2020-pcbs-and-heavy-metals-in-farmed-escaped-and">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Salmon, as sold from escaped farmed salmon caught at sea (Norway) had total arsenic higher at 1,680 µg/kg, against 860 µg/kg for farmed salmon (Norway) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2020-pcbs-and-heavy-metals-in-farmed-escaped-and|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2020-pcbs-and-heavy-metals-in-farmed-escaped-and">PCBs and Heavy Metals in Farmed, Escaped and Wild</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2020-pcbs-and-heavy-metals-in-farmed-escaped-and">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-salmon-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-salmon-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of salmon have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of salmon have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For total arsenic, the HMI reference median was lowest for salmon, as sold (47 µg/kg) and highest for salmon, cooked (240 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold or eaten, not uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Olmedo P, Pla A, Hernandez AF, Barbier F, Ayouni L, Gil F · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals">Determination of toxic elements (mercury, cadmium, lead, tin and arsenic) in fish and shellfish samples. Risk assessment for the consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environment International</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/olmedo2013-andalusia-fish-shellfish-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-salmon" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-salmon" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in salmon?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in salmon?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, salmon, as sold had the lowest total arsenic subgroup median in EURO (141 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (1,230 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For total mercury, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (10 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (70 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-salmon-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-salmon-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in salmon is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in salmon is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 11 results from 3 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" class="cite">[[sources/luvonga2021-seafood-arsenic-speciation|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Luvonga C, Rimmer CA, Yu LL, Lee SB · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/luvonga2021-seafood-arsenic-speciation">Determination of total arsenic and hydrophilic arsenic species in seafood</a></span><span
